content:
**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Green stem with surrounding yellow/senesced leaves and debris
- Key feature: gray, fluffy/cottony growth visible at the node junction where petiole meets stem
- Stem otherwise appears green and intact

**Diagnosis reasoning:**
The gray fluffy mycelial growth at the node is the hallmark early symptom of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum). The description states "gray to white lesions at nodes" and "fluffy, white growth on soybean stems." The test image shows exactly this — cottony gray fungal growth at a node, with the surrounding leaves yellowed, consistent with the disease progressing. The reference image shows a more advanced stage (bleached stem + black sclerotia), but the early-stage node infection matches.

Green_stem_disorder was considered (stem is still green while leaves are yellow), but the defining feature there is absence of external growth; the fluffy gray mycelium rules that out.

The symptom description matches: gray to white lesions at nodes on soybean stems. Surrounding yellowed leaves indicate late-season timing consistent with this disease."}
